chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding a man who died and left a will to a man, and upon the deceased man there was a debt, so the executor went and set aside that which was for the creditors, raised it in his house, and divided what remained among the heirs. If that which was for the creditors was stolen at night, from whom is it taken? He said: 'He is liable when he set it aside in his house; he pays from his own wealth.'
ai.seo_question: Who is liable if the creditor's share of an estate is stolen by the executor?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the executor is deemed personally liable (dhamin) for the stolen creditor funds because he segregated them, thereby assuming custodial responsibility (qabd) over that specific portion of the estate. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that voluntary segregation of assets creates a binding guarantee, distinguishing it from general estate management where liability might be limited. It underscores the importance of meticulous financial stewardship in Islamic inheritance law to protect creditors' rights.
